tier_reason: Upgraded from C: the README claims (1.5-4x, 18x) appear verbatim but without methodology, while the peer-reviewed paper 'Gradual Soundness: Lessons from Static Python' (The Art, Science, and Engineering of Programming 7(1):2, 2023; LaTeX source in brownplt/insta-model pj-7.1/paper.tex) gives 10-run timings with and without the Cinder JIT on public microbenchmarks (cinder/3.8 Tools/benchmarks). Not A: CPU model and compiler are not stated (only '64-bit CentOS Linux', 'default configure settings'), and the no-JIT baseline is Cinder's own build rather than stock CPython.

corrections.claimed_speedup: cinder/3.10 README: the JIT 'can achieve 1.5-4x speed improvements on many Python performance benchmarks'; 'Static Python plus Cinder JIT achieves 18x the performance of stock CPython on a typed version of the Richards benchmark'. Peer-reviewed paper appendix (Programming 2023, Cinder 3.8-era commits, mean of 10 runs, process user time): Cinder JIT with shadow frames on the original untyped benchmarks versus the same Cinder build with the JIT off: richards 3.8x, deltablue 1.9x, nbody 1.6x, fannkuch 1.5x; Static Python + JIT on the hand-optimized typed Richards (T-Max) versus untyped Richards without the JIT 17.7x, and on the simply-typed Richards (T-Min) about 7.2x (all derived from page data).
corrections.baseline: CPython interpreter: the same Cinder build with the JIT disabled (the README calls it stock CPython; the paper did not run a separate stock CPython build)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Paper: Cinder 'compiled with default configure settings', compiler not named; the cinder/3.10 README says its basic build instructions give a binary without PGO/LTO
corrections.hardware: 64-bit CentOS Linux system (paper); CPU model not stated
corrections.workload: Python microbenchmarks richards, deltablue, nbody and fannkuch (cinder/3.8 Tools/benchmarks, original untyped plus Static Python typed variants) run with the C++ method-at-a-time Cinder JIT (-X jit, JIT list limited to the benchmark code, with and without shadow frames), versus the same build with the JIT off; README additionally claims gains on unnamed 'Python performance benchmarks'.
corrections.caveats: The README numbers sit in the older cinder/3.10 branch (last commit 2024-06-25); the default branch meta/3.14 (last commit 2026-10-06) README says the name cinder is historical and points to facebookincubator/cinderx (MIT, 282 stars, a CPython 3.14+ extension) for the JIT and Static Python, so the JIT code now lives there. Paper timings are from Cinder 3.8 commits d0d071, c9d14c and 144a21 (2022), not the 3.10 branch. The no-JIT baseline is Cinder's own interpreter build, not stock CPython; no CPU model, compiler or PGO/LTO state given. The 18x needs hand-typed Static Python with primitive types (simply typed code gives about 7x); the 1.5-4x JIT range is backed by only four microbenchmarks in the paper. README: 'Is this supported? Short answer: no.' JIT-compiling every called function by default can make programs slower. No comparison with PyPy.

notes: Claims check out against the README and the peer-reviewed paper's appendix data; upgraded to B (paper co-authored by Brown University and Meta engineers). Shortcomings: baseline is Cinder with the JIT off rather than stock CPython, no CPU/compiler, 18x only for hand-optimized Static Python Richards, and the JIT has moved to facebookincubator/cinderx, which the orchestrator may want to note or list instead.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Toolchain clang/LLVM 6.0 per the README build instructions; flags used for the blog numbers not stated
corrections.caveats: Snippet only: numbers come from the first-party Quarkslab blog (EuroLLVM'18 / FOSDEM'18 era), which could not be opened; no CPU or flags. Harness flaws in benchmark/benchmark.cpp: Qsort tests 'if (cmp(v[i], v[left]))' where the K&R original tests '< 0', so with int_cmp returning -1/0/1 it is not a correct sort, and it re-sorts the same vector in place every iteration; BM_convolve allocates out with (n-3)^2 ints but the kernel writes index i*(n-m+1)+j up to (n-4)(n-1), out of bounds for every tested n (both the JIT and AOT paths run the same code, so the ratio is not fabricated, but the harness has undefined behaviour); the image is all zeros; JIT compile time is excluded from the timed loop. Baseline is AOT code of the same generic function, not PyPy, LuaJIT, V8 or HotSpot. Last commit 2021-05-15; needs an LLVM 6-era toolchain.
